summary: Decoded the 11 × 9-byte race base-stat table at DGROUP+0x52D9. Each race row is 8 ASCII-encoded attribute minimums + 1 null terminator. Decoder formula: byte - 0x41 ('A') = minimum stat value. KAR has no race-derived floor (always 0); KAR is rolled per-character at creation (a separate roll from the bonus-point pool). Data is loaded transiently into DGROUP when wpcmk_create_character_master runs (game_state=0x10); it is NOT populated at boot. Captured from save state with game_state=0x10 at the race-selection menu.
method: MCP dosbox_read_memory at physical offset 0x18048+0x52D9 = 0x1D321 (length 99 bytes), against a save state captured at the race-selection menu (game_state=0x10). The 11 race-table-base immediates pushed by stats_bump_to_racial_minimums callers (wpcmk file 0x2fdb..0x3041) confirmed the table base + 9-byte stride.

findings.claim: The 11-race attribute-floor table lives at DGROUP 0x52D9..0x5333+8, transiently populated during wpcmk character creation (game_state=0x10). Empty in any save captured before character creation runs.

addresses: file 0x2fdb: mov ax, 0x52d9; push ax; call stats_bump (race 0 / Human)
file 0x3041: mov ax, 0x5333 (race 10 / Mook, last entry)

findings.claim: Each race record is 9 bytes: 8 ASCII-encoded attribute-minimum bytes (STR, INT, PIE, VIT, DEX, SPD, PER, KAR) followed by 1 null terminator. Decoder: byte - 0x41 ('A') = minimum stat value. Confirmed by stats_bump_to_racial_minimums at wpcmk file 0x2c7b: instruction `add ax, 0xffbf` (= subtract 65) at file 0x2c91.
Decoded race base-stat table (race index, name, STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD/PER/KAR minimums).

KAR (Karma) attribute minimum is 0 for every race. Karma is rolled per-character at creation (a separate roll from the bonus-point pool — see 'personality reroll' state in the wpcmk-character-creation trace). Stock characters' decoded KAR values range from 3 (TREON) to 16 (TEMPEST), confirming per-character rolling rather than a fixed starting value.
Race base-stat decode is cross-validated against the 6 stock characters in pcfile.dbs. For each stock char, decoded character attributes = race base + class-favored bonus allocation.
verifications: THESUS race 0 Human, decoded char STR=18 vs Human STR base=9 → +9 bonus into STR (fighter optimization)
NOBAL race 1 Elf, decoded char PIE=13 vs Elf PIE base=10 → +3 into PIE (priest optimization)
NOBAL race 1 Elf, decoded char KAR=4 vs Elf KAR base=0 → +4 into KAR (karma-favoring priest)
PENTAG race 3 Gnome, decoded char INT=12 vs Gnome INT base=7 → +5 into INT (mage optimization)
PENTAG race 3 Gnome, decoded char KAR=9 vs Gnome KAR base=0 → +9 into KAR

findings.claim: The routine that LOADS this data into DGROUP at the start of character creation has not been identified. We know it's not winit state 0 (saves at later boot states have the region zeroed). Likely candidates: a wpcmk init routine, or a wroot helper called when wbase dispatches to game_state=0x10.

implications: An engine-faithful character-creation port can ship the decoded race base-stat table as a constant in @wiz6/data — no need to read from disk at runtime. The table is the engine's source of truth (cross-validated).

Future passes can apply the same MCP-read-memory technique to other transiently-populated wpcmk data: class skill bitmaps at wpcmk file 0x5cb8..0x5e93 (also DS-relative), class attribute requirements at 0x5e98.

The 'subtract 65' / ASCII-encoded-minimum representation generalizes — wpcmk's class requirement table likely uses the same encoding (already noted in docs/re/findings/wpcmk-state-machine-trace.json).
